quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 30 Questions • Passing Score 25

questions.question: When riding with a heavy load, you should adjust the:
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to match the heavier weight.

questions.question: The best lane position:

options.text: Is always the right portion of the lane.
Is always the center portion of the lane.
Is always the left portion of the lane.
Changes based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position based on road conditions, weather, and traffic around you.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict between motorcycles and other vehicles. Stay alert at intersections where another vehicle may cross your path.

questions.question: To reduce the time you need to react to a hazard, you should:

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit.

questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones and construction zones, keep your hands ready to use the clutch and brakes. This reduces your reaction time if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What should you do to stay in control while turning on a motorcycle?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Look ahead through the turn to plan your path.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to plan your path.
questions.explanation: To stay in control through a turn, look ahead by turning your head to see through the turn. Slow down before turning and lean your motorcycle as needed.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle with a sidecar, where should the passenger sit?

options.text: Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Neither on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.

questions.explanation: The passenger should ride in the sidecar. They must keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect you?

options.text: They make you unable to focus.

questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, or nerves cause drowsiness and can affect your ability to ride safely. Know how any medication affects you before riding.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, which of the following is NOT important?
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly and have no visible damage, such as cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. Appearance is not important for safety.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance:

options.text: When roads are wet or icy.
When it is colder than usual.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: When roads are wet or icy.
questions.explanation: Normally, keep a two-second distance from the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance when conditions make it harder to stop, such as wet or icy roads.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best traction?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers provide poor traction. Dry pavement is the safest surface for a motorcycle.

questions.question: Face shields and goggles:

options.text: Will almost never need to be replaced.
Will get scratched and become weak over time, so you need to replace them often.
Should be made of material that breaks easily during a crash.
Should block all air from passing through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will get scratched and become weak over time, so you need to replace them often.
questions.explanation: Face shields and goggles are made of plastic. They get scratched and become weak as time goes by. Replace them regularly to keep them working well and stay comfortable.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Can make a rider look good.
Is usually too hot to wear while riding.
Should never be worn while riding.

questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket, ideally made of leather, when riding for safety. In warm weather, a leather jacket can also help prevent dehydration. Many motorcycle jackets are made to keep you cool even in hot weather.

questions.question: If you brake while in a curve:

options.text: It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You have more grip as you lean into the curve.
You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. Your tires use some of their grip to make the turn while the motorcycle is leaning. This means less grip is available for braking.

questions.question: If you are riding in traffic when a small animal enters your lane, you should:

options.text: Do whatever you can, including swerving into other lanes, to avoid the animal.
Change lanes as fast as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.explanation: Try to avoid hitting an animal if you can do so safely. If you are in traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane can cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is less dangerous than hitting another car.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard to see at night. To stay safe, a motorcycle rider should:

options.text: Slow down when riding at night.
Honk their horn over and over when riding at night.
Ride directly in front of another vehicle so their headlights light you up at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when riding at night.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down and increase your distance from other vehicles. Use the headlights of cars ahead to see farther down the road. Use your high beam headlight when it is safe to do so. Be ready to adjust your position in your lane as needed.

questions.question: A motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Can tip over if you turn too fast.
Is made to take corners at any speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can tip over if you turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels on the ground, a sidecar can tip over if you turn it too sharply or go too fast around a corner.

questions.question: When you ride a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Turn your whole head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn by moving only your head. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help you stay balanced while turning. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black words or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black words or symbols. They alert drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: In any crash, you have a better chance of staying safe if you do all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: You can lower your risk of injury by wearing an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: When someone is following you too closely, you should:

options.text: Do not worry about them and focus on the road ahead.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle someone following too closely is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will make them follow you at higher speeds, which is more dangerous. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers do not expect you to be there and may suddenly leave the road.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what is the correct rule?

options.text: You can complete the pass in a no passing zone.
You can go up to 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You must complete the pass on the shoulder if one exists.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: Passing must happen only in areas where it is safe and legal. You must follow the speed limit while passing.

questions.question: How can over-the-counter drugs affect riding?

options.text: They only affect riding if you drink alcohol at the same time.
They affect everyone in the same way.

questions.explanation: Many drugs, including over-the-counter and prescription medications, can impair your ability to ride safely. This is similar to how alcohol affects riding.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's total braking power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When should a group of riders merge onto a highway?
questions.explanation: Use a single-file formation when merging onto a highway, turning, or taking curves. A staggered formation is better for normal riding conditions.

questions.question: Which item should you NOT check during a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil, fluids, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: How can you make night riding safer?

options.text: Avoid riding at night whenever possible.
Night riding is unsafe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Only ride at night in the city.

questions.explanation: Wearing reflective materials makes you more visible to other drivers when riding at night.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Keep them busy with other activities.
Keep them from leaving until they are sober.

questions.explanation: Never allow an impaired friend to ride. Arrange another way for them to get home, involve them in other activities, or ask them to stay until they are sober.

questions.question: How should riders choose their lane position?

options.text: Pick one position and always use it.
Change positions often to stay alert.
Choose the position that gives you the most space around you.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose the position that gives you the most space around you.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly. Choose the lane position that gives you the most space and makes you most visible to other drivers.

questions.question: How do curved mirrors make cars appear?
questions.explanation: Curved mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors, but objects appear to be farther away than they actually are.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, where should you position yourself in your lane?

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Use your rearview mirrors more often than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay on the side of your lane away from the parked cars. This protects you from opened car doors or people stepping out between cars.
